rows.description: A child struggles to grasp quantity, time and money, and feels panic in maths lessons though good at language or art. Hands-on materials, patient repetition and no shaming allow progress.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A parent worries about grades and other people's comments and feels torn between pushing and protecting. Working with the school, keeping the child's confidence up and celebrating other talents keeps the family steady.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A teenager may think in pictures, tell stories brilliantly and struggle with spelling and reading speed under time limits. Getting an assessment and permitted accommodations shows what they truly know.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22

rows.subtype: Teacher noticing a gap between effort and results [Observer]
rows.description: A teacher sees strong oral answers but weak written work, or careful effort with number errors. Suggesting screening, avoiding reading aloud on the spot and valuing ideas separate learning difference from lack of effort.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22

rows.description: A young adult uses audio books, voice tools and extra time, and feels embarrassed at first to ask. Sharing the difference with tutors and employers usually earns understanding and shows real ability.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: A toddler screams at hand dryers, refuses certain textures or seeks constant spinning and crashing. The body handles input differently, and calm environments with gentle exposure suit better than force.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child cannot bear tags, bright lights, the canteen smell or the school bell, and appears irritable or withdrawn. The discomfort is real, and small changes like a quiet seat or headphones help a lot.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Family member misreading it as fussiness [Receiver]
rows.description: A parent or relative may think the child is picky or dramatic about clothes or food. Listening, believing the child and trying small adjustments reduces daily battles.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A teenager may chew, fidget and crave loud music, while another covers ears in a crowd and avoids certain foods. Both are managing their nervous system, and self-knowledge lets them plan.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 18–22

rows.description: A young adult learns their triggers and chooses seating, clothing and routines to ease them, and explains needs briefly to others. Accommodation is self-care, not fussiness.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17
